before.title: The Hecke sign automorphism, pullback and contragredient dual
before.statement:
For every commutative $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive $R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with $\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.
2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying $R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$ is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.
3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with $(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.
4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit $q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.
before.strategy:
(1) Since $T_i^{-1}=q^{-1}T_i+(q^{-1}-1)$, one has $-qT_i^{-1}=(q-1)-T_i$; the assignment $T_i\mapsto(q-1)-T_i$ exchanges the two roots $q$ and $-1$ of the quadratic relation and preserves the braid and distant-commutation relations, so it defines an algebra endomorphism; $\theta^2$ fixes every generator, hence $\theta^2=\mathrm{id}$. For a reduced word, $\theta(T_w)=\prod_j((q-1)-T_{i_j})=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{i_1}^{-1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}^{-1}=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$. Since $*$ fixes each $T_i$ and $\theta$ is built from the generators, $\theta$ commutes with $*$. Base change is immediate from the formulas.

(2) Functoriality of pullback along an involutive automorphism is formal; exactness of $(-)^\theta$ is exactness of the identity functor with a twisted action, and submodules, quotients, composition multiplicities and simplicity are unchanged because the underlying lattices and inclusion relations are unchanged.

(3) $(f\cdot h)(m)=f(mh^*)$ is a right action because $**=\mathrm{id}$; for finite free $M$ the dual basis computes the rank and all assertions are preserved by base change. The equality $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$ is the computation $(f\cdot h)(m)=f(m\theta(h^*))=(f\theta(h))(m)$, using that $\theta$ commutes with $*$.

(4) It suffices to prove $\theta(x_{(m)})=q^{\binom m2}y_{(m)}$ for one row: the row subgroup $S_\lambda$ is a direct product of symmetric groups on disjoint intervals, the corresponding $x$- and $y$-elements multiply, and $\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}{2}=\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))$. Work over the fraction field $K=\mathbb Q(q)$ of $A=\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$, where $H_K$ is split semisimple (Hoefsmit's theorem; Mathas, manuscript, Corollary 3.22 (Hoefsmit), printed p. 26). Since $T_ix_{(m)}=qx_{(m)}$ by [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]], one computes $T_i\theta(x_{(m)})=\theta(\theta(T_i)x_{(m)})=\theta(((q-1)-T_i)x_{(m)})=\theta(-x_{(m)})=-\theta(x_{(m)})$; hence $\theta(x_{(m)})$ lies in the space of vectors killed by all $T_i+1$, which is the sign isotypic component of the left regular representation of the split semisimple $H_K$ and is one-dimensional, spanned by the nonzero element $y_{(m)}$. So $\theta(x_{(m)})=cy_{(m)}$ for some $c\in K^\times$. Apply the algebra character $\rho_-:H_K\to K$, $T_i\mapsto-1$ (well defined because $(-1)^2=(q-1)(-1)+q$). Then $\rho_-(\theta(x_{(m)}))=\sum_{w\in S_m}q^{\ell(w)}$ and $\rho_-(y_{(m)})=\sum_{w\in S_m}q^{-\ell(w)}$, so $c=\prod_{k=1}^m\frac{1+q+\cdots+q^{k-1}}{1+q^{-1}+\cdots+q^{-(k-1)}}=q^{\binom m2}$. Both sides of $\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda$ now hold in $H_K$; as they are elements of the free $A$-submodule $H_A$ and $H_A\hookrightarrow H_K$, they hold over $A$, hence over every $R$ by the base change $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto q$. The companion identity follows by applying $\theta$ again. At $q=1$ the formula reads $\theta(T_w)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}$, the pullback along the sign automorphism. Sources: Mathas, manuscript, Notes on Chapter 3, Notes 3 and 4 (printed pp. 34--35), which record the $\#$ automorphism and $m_\lambda^\#=q^an_\lambda$ and cite Murphy's proof; that citation is not used here, the argument above is the replacement, with Hoefsmit's Corollary 3.20 supplying the split semisimplicity. KMR, (3.14) and §8 (Theorem 8.5), contain the parallel sign automorphism and its role in the signed-conjugate comparison, read as an analogue. No choice principle is used.

after.strategy:
The quadratic relation gives $T_i^{-1}=q^{-1}(T_i-(q-1))$, so $\theta(T_i)=-qT_i^{-1}=(q-1)-T_i$. Inverses satisfy the braid and distant-commutation relations, so their uniform scalar multiples do too; the quadratic relation is preserved by interchanging its roots $q,-1$. Applying $\theta$ twice fixes every generator. Hence it is an involutive algebra automorphism, and it commutes with star because both constructions fix the reversed generator relations. On a reduced word, $\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$. All these formulas are universal and survive base change.
For pullback, $\theta$ is onto, so a subspace or submodule is stable for the new action exactly when it was stable for the old action. The same underlying inclusion and quotient maps prove exactness, all submodule/radical/simple and composition-series claims, and twisting twice is identity. The action $(f\cdot h)(m)=f(mh^*)$ satisfies $((f\cdot h)\cdot k)(m)=f(mk^*h^*)=f(m(hk)^*)$. For finite free modules, the dual basis identifies base changes, and commuting $\theta$ with star proves $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.
To compute $\theta(x_\lambda)$ without any generic semisimplicity, use its left $-1$ eigenvalue for each parabolic generator: $T_i\theta(x_\lambda)=\theta(((q-1)-T_i)x_\lambda)=-\theta(x_\lambda)$. If $a=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}a_wT_w$ is such a common eigenvector, pairing $w,s_iw$ with $\ell(s_iw)=\ell(w)+1$ in the standard multiplication formula gives $qa_{s_iw}=-a_w$. Thus $a_w=(-q)^{-\ell(w)}a_1$ by a finite reduced word; the common eigenspace is the free line $Ry_\lambda$ over every ring, without dividing by $q+1$ or a quantum factorial. For the longest parabolic word $w_0$ of length $N$, expand each product $\theta(T_w)=\prod_j((q-1)-T_{i_j})$. Its unique top-length standard term is $(-1)^{\ell(w)}T_w$; any omitted letter has fewer factors and cannot create length $N$. Consequently the coefficient of $T_{w_0}$ in $\theta(x_\lambda)$ is $(-1)^N$. In $cy_\lambda$ it is $c(-q)^{-N}$, so $c=q^N$, using only this unit. Thus $\theta(x_\lambda)=q^Ny_\lambda$ and applying $\theta$ again gives $\theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-N}x_\lambda$. At $q=1$, $T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}=T_w$, so $\theta(T_w)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}T_w$: it is sign pullback, not inversion of the permutation. Empty and singleton cases have $N=0$. No choice principle is used.

before.title: The permutation form is H-contravariant and restricts to the DJ form
before.statement:
In the notation of [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], for every commutative $R$ and $q\in R^\times$, the permutation form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ is well defined, symmetric and $R$-bilinear, with $\beta(x_\lambda T_d,x_\lambda T_e)=\delta_{d,e}q^{\ell(d)}$ on the distinguished basis of [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]]. It is $H$-contravariant:
$$\beta(xh,y)=\beta(x,yh^*)\qquad(x,y\in M(\lambda),\ h\in H).$$
Its restriction $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ to the polytabloid module $P(\lambda)$ satisfies the same identity for $x,y\in P(\lambda)$ and is called the DJ form. Both $\beta$ and $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ are compatible with every base change $R\to R'$. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Well-definedness, symmetry and bilinearity are immediate from the freeness of the distinguished basis [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]](1). By additivity in $x$ and $y$ it suffices to verify contravariance for $x=x_\lambda T_d$, $y=x_\lambda T_e$ and $h=T_i$ (generators), and the identity extends to words by induction. Writing $t=t^\lambda\cdot d$, $u=t^\lambda\cdot e$, one distinguishes the three positions of the pair $(i,i+1)$ in $t$ and in $u$, using the action rules of [[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]](3) on the left and on the right. In each of the resulting cases the same-row/same-column and length-change conditions for $t$ and $u$ are linked by the relations $d'=e\Leftrightarrow d=e'$ and $d\,s_i=e$, and one checks term by term that the two sides either both vanish or that the $q$ and $(q-1)$ coefficients combine; for example, when $t\cdot s_i$ is row standard with $\ell(d')>\ell(d)$ and $u\cdot s_i$ is row standard with $\ell(e')<\ell(e)$, the identity reduces to $\delta_{d',e}q^{\ell(d')}=q\delta_{d,e'}q^{\ell(d)}+(q-1)\delta_{d,e}q^{\ell(d)}$, and the incompatible subcase analysis leaves only the two mutually exclusive configurations in which both sides vanish, while when $u\cdot s_i$ is not row standard or $u\cdot s_i$ is standard with the same length direction, the two sides are visibly equal. This is the standard verification that the q-permutation form is contravariant; the same case split is what underlies the classical tabloid form of [[def-integral-tabloid-bilinear-form-and-specht-gram-matrix]] at $q=1$. The restriction statement is by definition of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$; base change is immediate from the formula. No step assumes that $\beta$ or its restriction is nondegenerate. No choice principle is used.

after.strategy: The distinguished row basis is proved free, so the diagonal weights $q^{\ell(d)}$ define the stated symmetric bilinear form. For each generator $T_i$, the row tabloids split into singleton orbits (same row, action scalar $q$) and two-element swap orbits. Order a swap pair with the shorter representative first. Its right-action matrix is $A_i=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\q&q-1\end{pmatrix}$ and its Gram matrix is $D=\operatorname{diag}(q^a,q^{a+1})$. Direct multiplication gives $A_iD=DA_i^{\mathsf T}$; singleton blocks satisfy the same equality, and different blocks are orthogonal. Thus $\beta(xT_i,y)=\beta(x,yT_i)$ for all row-module vectors. Iteration over a generator word, reversing the word on the second side, gives $\beta(xh,y)=\beta(x,yh^*)$ for every $h$. Restriction to the actual submodule $P(\lambda)$ is contravariant. All coordinates and structure constants are universal Laurent polynomials, so the whole proof survives arbitrary base change. Nondegeneracy of the restricted form is not asserted and no choice is used.

before.title: The Murphy cellular basis, the cell law and the Murphy form
before.statement:
For every commutative $R$, $q\in R^\times$, and $\lambda\vdash n$ with its row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an $R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.
2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and $I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$ (dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.
3. The **Murphy cell module** $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.
4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with $m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is symmetric, associative in the sense $G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.
5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every base change.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank $f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|=\dim S^\lambda_{\mathbb Q(q)}$. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: This is the integral Murphy theory, assembled from the two independent treatments read for this page. Mathas, manuscript, §3: Lemma 3.2 and Proposition 3.3 (row-coset bookkeeping), Lemma 3.12 (the Garnir relation $m_{t^\lambda g}=\sum_{\tau\rhd g}m_{t^\lambda\tau}+h$ with $h$ in higher-shape row-standard spans), Lemma 3.14 (straightening of $m_{st}$ in terms of standard tableaux and higher shapes), Corollary 3.15 (the fixed-first-index multiplication rule modulo the higher ideal), Theorem 3.18 (Murphy Basis Theorem; the basis statement is assembled on printed p. 23 from the Garnir straightening plus the RSK rank count $\sum_\lambda(f^\lambda)^2=n!$, and item (ii) there is the cell law), with Corollary 3.17 for the two-sidedness of the ideals. The general cellular-language assertions, the form $G_\lambda$, its symmetry, associativity and the radical being a submodule, are the Graham-Lehrer theory as recalled in Chapter 2 of the manuscript (Proposition 2.7 for the symmetry and associativity of the cell form and for the radical being a submodule), instantiated at this basis; the form is concretely the coefficient of $x_\lambda$ in $x_\lambda T_{d(s)}T_{d(t)^{-1}}x_\lambda$ expanded in the standard basis, as in Ryom-Hansen, arXiv:0904.4243v5, §2 (PDF p. 6) (where $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, the standard elements $x_{st}$, the dominance ideals $N^\lambda$, the module $S^A_q(\lambda)$, the action rules (6) and the Garnir relations (9) are stated in the same normalization). Everything is defined over $A=\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$ and the basis statements hold after every base change; \emph{no generic semisimplicity, no division by quantum factorials and no rank count over $\mathbb Q$ is used for the integral assertions}, which come from the integral straightening. The higher ideals are two-sided because of the star symmetry and the straightening; this is Corollary 3.17 of the manuscript. No choice principle is used.

# Standalone integral Murphy cellular basis and form

Same author/run/construction scope as `constructive-proof.md`. This is a research-only complete proof candidate for the formerly sketch-only NEW50 premise. Source actually read: Mathas manuscript PDF objects27–36, printed18–27, in `/tmp/b50/sources/mathas_raw_pages.json`; its printed21–25 Garnir/lex basis proof is reconstructed below. The dominance upgrade here is a new trace argument using the already proved local opposite-dominance double-coset zero, rather than importing Mathas Proposition3.16 or a source20 prototype.

## Required independent published/local premises

Published IDs whose actual statements were read:

- `def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra` and `thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra`: standard basis, quadratic and braid relations, inversion length, multiplication rule. The standard-basis theorem is published; its current carrier has a judge stamp rather than a delegated audit. This is disclosed, not upgraded here.
- `def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape` and `def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition`: partitions, row/standard tableaux, conjugation.
- `cor-sum-of-squares-of-standard-tableau-numbers`: Σλ(f^λ)^2=n! for every n≥0, including the empty shape. Published independent source is `thm-robinson-schensted-correspondence`, not source20.

Local elementary prerequisites proved here or in companion `constructive-proof.md`: row-permutation-module basis/action; sign automorphism θ; minimal parabolic and double-coset sorting; opposite-dominance zero xκHyρ=0 when κ is not dominated by ρ'. None uses the Murphy basis. Thus the proposed dependency graph has no cycle: double-coset zero → this Murphy lemma → DJ split basis → comparison/form theorems.

Use A=Z[q,q^{-1}], arbitrary specialization to R, n≥0, right modules, xα=Σw∈SαT_w for compositions α. For row-standard α-tableaux s,t set m_st^α=T_dα(s)^* xα T_dα(t). The involution star fixes generators and reverses products. For partitions, use lexicographic order temporarily; dominance replaces it in Section6. Empty and singleton shapes have x=1, one tableau, H=R and all claims below reduce to multiplication in R.

## 1. Row modules and elementary ordering facts

Sorting labels inside each row gives one representative dα(t) per right coset Sαd; inversion counting gives ell(ad)=ell(a)+ell(d) for a∈Sα. Pairing terms w and ws_i in xα gives xαT_i=qxα for every adjacent generator inside Sα. Thus b_t=xαT_dα(t) form a basis of xαH: each expands with disjoint standard-basis support Sαd, with coefficient1 at T_d. The right action is q b_t if i,i+1 lie in the same row, b_{ts_i} if the swapped tableau is row-standard and its length increases, and q b_{ts_i}+(q−1)b_t if length decreases. These assertions also follow immediately by row sorting and the standard Hecke multiplication rule. The left counterparts follow by star.

For row-standard tableaux define t≥u if every initial-label row composition of t dominates that of u. We need the following elementary support lemma: if v>g, d(t)=d(g)w and ell(d(t))=ell(d(g))+ell(w), then b_vT_w has support strictly more dominant than t. No Bruhat theorem is needed. Choose a reduced word for w; the successive tableaux starting at g and ending at t are row-standard. Indeed each length-increasing adjacent-label interchange adds one inverted pair of row-reading nodes and removes none; a within-row inversion could never disappear before the final tableau t, which has none. Thus each step is an increasing-length row-standard swap s→s'=s s_i, with i in an upper row a and i+1 in a lower row b>a; s' is less dominant than s.

For any r≥s, both row tabloids r and r s_i dominate s'. Only the label cutoff m=i needs checking. For row cutoffs k<a, use `count_{≤i}(r s_i;first k rows)≥count_{≤i−1}(r;first k rows)≥count_{≤i−1}(s;first k rows)=count_{≤i}(s';first k rows)`. For k≥b use `count_{≤i}(r s_i;first k rows)≥count_{≤i+1}(r;first k rows)−1≥count_{≤i+1}(s;first k rows)−1=count_{≤i}(s';first k rows)`. For a≤k<b use the first bound again, since s' contains neither label i at that cutoff and `count_{≤i}(s')=count_{≤i−1}(s)`. Unchanged cutoffs inherit the old dominance; row sorting changes none of these counts. The unswapped r already dominates s≥s'. If r>s, neither output tabloid can equal s': the unswapped source s' was below s and absent, and a swapped source equal to s' would have to be s's_i=s. Therefore each multiplication step takes support strictly above s to support strictly above s'. Induction along the reduced word proves the support lemma with strictness and all coefficients over A. This is a direct replacement for the Bruhat-based Mathas Corollary3.8.

## 2. Reordering composition shapes

If β is obtained by rearranging parts of α, choose the permutation d carrying whole α-row blocks, in their internal increasing order, to the corresponding β-row blocks. Both d and d^{-1} are distinguished representatives for these row groups. They conjugate Sβ to Sα, and inversion counting gives xαT_d=T_dxβ.
